title: Round‑trip parse-and-repair benchmark for low-bit function-call outputs
creator: Aisha Kumar
body:
Summary:
We need a deterministic benchmark and CI-grade harness that evaluates how FP8/INT8 quantization profiles affect structured function-call outputs, but with an emphasis on detection + automated lightweight repair (round‑trip parse -> repair -> reserialize) rather than only measuring raw schema failures. The goal is to characterize failure modes introduced by low-bit quantization (token drop/shift, numerical truncation of structured fields, punctuation corruption) and validate if an automated repair stage can recover semantically-correct, schema-conformant payloads without masking underlying model regressions.

Motivation:
- Existing tests flag schema violations but don't quantify reparability or the risk of silent semantic changes after 'repair'.
- For Dedicated/Private customers running aggressive quant profiles, we must provide actionable remediation (repair heuristics) and clear CI gating signals (pass/fail thresholds + degradation metrics) to avoid regressions in production integrations that rely on function calls.

Scope / Deliverables:
1) A synthetic workload generator that emits function-call prompts and golden responses across 4 axes: nested JSON depth, long string fields (escape-heavy), numeric precision-sensitive fields (timestamps/coordinates), and enumerated token-constrained fields (enums). Include real customer-derived prompt seeds (anonymized) plus randomized fuzz corpus.
2) Round‑trip harness: call model under target quant profiles -> capture raw token stream -> attempt parse into JSON schema -> if parse fails, run the lightweight repair engine -> reserialize and compare to golden canonical. The repair engine will include: bracket/quote balancing, punctuation normalization, enum soft-match (Levenshtein + token-probability heuristic), and numeric clamp/round heuristics.
3) Metrics and scoring: schema-conformance rate, reparability rate (portion of failed parses recovered to valid JSON), semantic-fidelity score (field-level diffs weighted by customer-criticality), and token-provenance delta (where in token offsets corruption occurs).
4) CI integration: a Jenkins/Buildkite job that runs the benchmark for every quant profile change and fails when schema-conformance drops below 99.5% AND reparability is below 90% for production profiles. Add a soft-warning channel for experimental profiles.
5) Dashboarding: time-series of failure modes by profile + example digest of repair attempts (before/after, diff). Hook into Console's rollouts dashboard for correlated alerts.

Design notes / tradeoffs:
- Repair should be conservative: prefer to surface uncertain repairs in the diff rather than silently rewrite enums. Repairs will attach an uncertainty score.
- We will not use large secondary LMs for repair (too heavy for CI); instead use determinist and lightweight heuristics with configurable thresholds. A later RFC can explore a small verifier model if heuristics are insufficient.
- We must ensure the harness captures low-latency failure modes: token truncation at different cache sequence lengths, shifted KV cache effects when switching from FP32 to FP8, and batch-token interleaving noise.

Acceptance criteria:
- Benchmark generates at least 10k unique function-call cases covering the 4 axes and edge cases.
- A single CI run across the production FP8 and INT8 profiles completes in <30m on dedicated infra.
- For the baseline (current pre-quant) model, reparability >= 99% and semantic-fidelity score >= 0.995 (on the canonical set).
- For each target quant profile, we produce a report that lists top-5 failure classes and an actionable remediation: adjust quant scale, add prefix caching, or tune beam/temperature.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: corpus generator + canonical case selection + schema inventory (owner: Jonas).
- Week 2: implement parse/repair engine + unit tests for heuristics (owner: Aisha).
- Week 3: integrate model inference under quant profiles + data capture pipeline (owner: infra-eval team).
- Week 4: CI job and dashboard integration + stakeholder demo.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFER/Roundtrip+Repair+Benchmark (draft)
- Golden corpus (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/roundtrip-golden-corpus (access: internal)
- Prototype PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-eval/pull/512
- Dashboard mockup: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/roundtrip-repair/quant-harness

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: repair masks regressions and teams ship with degraded semantics. Mitigation: make repair score visible in CI and add gating rule that any repaired request in production must be logged and sampled for manual review for 7 days.
- Risk: CI runtime grows too large. Mitigation: run full corpus nightly and a focused smoke subset on PRs.

Next steps / immediate tasks:
- (Jonas) finalize schema inventory and pick initial 2 customer seed prompts by 2026-02-28.
- (Aisha) land parse+repair library skeleton and unit tests by 2026-03-05.
- (Infra) provision 1 GPU host for profiling quant runs by 2026-03-03.
comments: 2026-02-26 - Jonas Reed: Kickoff meeting done; agreed to prioritize branded-enum cases (payment_status, currency) and timestamp precision because customers reported regressions.
2026-03-02 - Aisha Kumar: Initial parse+repair library landed in the feature branch. Basic bracket/quote rebalancer and enum soft-match implemented. Unit tests added for 120 cases.
2026-03-06 - Infra: GPU host spun up (g4dn-like); but observed higher variance in tokenization offsets when batch size >8. Added to risk log.
2026-03-10 - Review (PM - Carlos Mendes): Please add a clear operator-visible flag when repair is applied; PMs want to avoid silent fixes for billing-related fields.
2026-03-12 - Jonas Reed: Updated CI job to emit repaired examples to an artifact store and added a quick viewer for diffs. Preparing demo for Platform Sync.
2026-03-12 - Aisha Kumar: Note: we discovered one failure mode where numeric exponent tokens are split across two token ids under INT8 profile; adding a specialized numeric-rejoin heuristic.
